summary: Qualified a genuinely Rust/OXC, non-fork architecture at canonical OXC commit 8e0ed2ebb96137fb1611cdbd5742d5cb46037d40. The disposable spike compiled canonical parser/AST/semantic/linter/formatter crates, ran a real built-in OXC rule on both same-width-normalized TSRX and an externally built arena AST with original spans, printed custom TSRX IR through OXC formatter-core, and round-tripped a marked full-Oxfmt projection back to @{/@if syntax. Current Vite+ project-local oxlint/oxfmt resolution makes literal vp lint/fmt/check integration practical; the official editor finds those binaries but still needs a thin .tsrx selector client. One native projection buffer is allowed only on TSRX and measured at 94.2% of direct parse throughput in the memory-traffic control; ordinary JS/TS bypasses it.
rationale: The earlier crates.io-only assumption was disproved: canonical oxc_linter 1.74.0, oxc_formatter 0.59.0, and oxc_formatter_core 0.59.0 set publish=false. Exact-revision Cargo dependencies on their public canonical Git workspace crates compile without copying, patching, or forking OXC and pin installed artifacts against upstream breakage. Rejecting that boundary would force either a process wrapper or a fork and would not meet the owner's intended in-process OXC toolchain.
